name: Deepgram Aura (text-to-speech)
positioning: Deepgram's text-to-speech line (Aura, Aura-2 and the newer Flux TTS) sits alongside its speech-to-text and Voice Agent APIs on one developer platform.

pricing.model: Pay-as-you-go per character, with discounted Growth plan rates for annual prepaid commitments.
pricing.headline: Aura-2 is $0.030 per 1K characters ($30 per 1M) pay-as-you-go; Flux TTS $45 per 1M; Aura (first generation) $15 per 1M.
pricing.headlineTier: Aura-2, Pay As You Go (widest-language model; Flux TTS is English-only and recommended by Deepgram for new builds at $45)

tiers.name: Flux TTS (Pay As You Go)
tiers.notes: English-only today, served on /v2/speak; $45 also confirmed on the Flux product page.

tiers.name: Aura-2 (Pay As You Go)
tiers.notes: Seven languages; $30 also confirmed on the Aura-2 launch article.

tiers.name: Aura (Pay As You Go)
tiers.notes: First-generation, English voices only. Single-source (pricing page).

pricing.freeTier: $200 free credit on sign-up, no credit card required, then pay-as-you-go (credit applies to all products, not TTS only).
promotions: Flux TTS credit match: for every $1 spent on Flux TTS, $1 in credits is added, up to $500; Pay As You Go and Growth plans; offer ends 2026-12-31.
Flux TTS free build period (up to 45 concurrent streams) ran through 2026-09-12; standard pricing applies since 2026-09-13 (already ended).

voices.count: Docs catalog lists roughly 36 Flux TTS English voices, about 90 Aura-2 voices across 7 languages and 12 first-generation Aura English voices (counted from the voice catalog page text, approximate).
voices.languages: Flux TTS: English only (several accents). Aura-2: English, Spanish, German, French, Dutch, Italian, Japanese. Aura: English.

streaming.vendorStatedLatency: Vendor-stated: Flux TTS output starts 'in as low as 80 ms'. Not independently measured.

compatibility.note: Deepgram uses its own /v1/speak (Aura) and /v2/speak (Flux TTS) endpoints with 'Authorization: Token' auth and the voice chosen via the model query parameter; no OpenAI-style speech route was found in the pages read.

licensing.attributionOrConditions: Model Improvement Program opt-out parameter (mip_opt_out) exists; docs note pricing impacts of opting out.

limits.concurrency: Pay As You Go, North America: Aura and Aura-2 up to 15 concurrent REST and 45 concurrent streaming requests; Flux TTS 15 REST / 45 streaming in North America and 5 in other listed regions.

compliance.note: Self-attested on the pricing page: SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2, HIPAA compliant, GDPR with an EU endpoint (api.eu.deepgram.com). Flux TTS page also mentions cloud, private cloud or on-prem deployment.

strengths.claim: Aura-2 supports seven languages; Flux TTS is a newer English model built for streaming voice agents with interruption reporting.
Vendor states Flux TTS output starts in as low as 80 ms (vendor-stated).
Offers speech-to-text, TTS and a Voice Agent API on one platform with a single account and API key.
Publishes SOC 2, HIPAA and GDPR statements and a dedicated EU endpoint.
Low entry price: Aura (first generation) is $15 per 1M characters and Aura-2 is $30 per 1M, with a $200 free credit.

limitations.claim: Flux TTS (the recommended newer model) is English-only today; other languages require Aura-2.
The Flux TTS credit-match promotion ends 2026-12-31 and the free build period ended 2026-09-12.

stepsToMove: Replace POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/speak?model=aura-2-<voice>-<lang> (or /v2/speak for Flux TTS) with ReadAloud's speech endpoint.
Move the text from the JSON body field 'text' to the corresponding ReadAloud input field; pick a ReadAloud voice instead of the Deepgram model string in the query.
Replace the 'Authorization: Token' header with the ReadAloud bearer key.
Map Deepgram's encoding/container/sample_rate/bit_rate query parameters to ReadAloud's response format option.
For streaming, replace the wss /v1/speak or /v2/speak message flow (Speak, Flush, Clear) with ReadAloud's WebSocket or HTTP streaming.
Voices and languages may not map one to one; Deepgram voices do not carry over.

bestFor: Teams already using Deepgram for transcription or its Voice Agent API who want TTS on the same platform, plus developers needing a low per-character price (Aura) or multiple European and Japanese languages (Aura-2).
